text:
maria: found during vuln triage: on-prem agent (customer: ACME-staging) exposes a local management endpoint on 127.0.0.1:2379 that accepts unauthenticated requests. KMS proxying possible from there. major risk if a jumpbox or pod is compromised.
jess: yikes. can you show repro and how bad is it?
maria: repro: exec into agent pod, `curl http://127.0.0.1:2379/keys` -> 200 with JSON payload. Severity: High for pinned on-prem installs.
kevin: this sounds like legacy agent v1.3 we deprecated last quarter?
maria: correct. customer pinned to v1.3 so earlier default-disable didn't apply.
ryan: immediate mitigations: 1) apply a restrictive NetworkPolicy denying egress from agent pods except to internal KMS endpoints; 2) tighten the service account RBAC to only allow minimal KMS RPCs; 3) enable KMS audit logging and stream to secure sink; 4) rotate potentially exposed keys ASAP.
jess: I can apply a canary netpol to their cluster if they grant access. we should also add an admission webhook that blocks agent images < v1.4.
kevin: agree. additionally enforce mTLS between agent and KMS and require VPC-level egress whitelisting so nodes cannot reach public endpoints.
sec-bot: [automated] created ticket SEC-2026-1893: "onprem agent management endpoint exposed" (priority P0).
maria: proposed plan: a) immediate canary netpol + RBAC tighten, b) require customer rotate KMS keys and enable audit streaming to our secure sink, c) ship hotfix v1.4.1 disabling mgmt endpoint by default + mTLS, d) evaluate forced upgrades for pinned installs after legal sign-off.
ryan: i'll own the incident runbook and oncall coordination. ETA: can push netpol in ~30m if customer approves; prepping pre-approved commands now.
jess: i'll draft the customer support note with exact logs and verification steps plus a postmortem template.
kevin: we should collect: node iptables dump, VPC flow logs for suspicious egress, and KMS audit trail (request IDs).
maria: minimal audit fields to collect: `timestamp`, `src_ip`, `service_account`, `pod_name`, `path`, `response_code`, `kms_key_id`, `request_body_sha256`. route them to splunk/secure-sink and tag SEC-2026-1893.
ryan: also add an admission policy snippet to block agent containers running as `privileged` or using `hostNetwork: true`.
jess: legal question: do we have authority to force upgrades on pinned customers in critical security incidents? current policy requires opt-in. legal needs to review emergency forced-upgrade clause.
maria: for now we'll provide an assisted one-time upgrade offer and hotfix. escalate legal for policy change in parallel.
kevin: quick canary NetworkPolicy snippet: 
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: restrict-redwood-agent-egress
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          redwood-kms: "internal"
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
kevin: and the kubectl commands: `kubectl -n redwood apply -f canary-netpol.yaml && kubectl label ns redwood-kms redwood-kms=internal`
sec-bot: [automated] incident INC-2026-0789 created; owner: ryan. paging oncall.
deploy-bot: [automated] flagged cluster acme-staging for manual intervention; autopromote disabled for pinned clusters.
ryan: pager ack. assignment: triage=maria, mitigation=kevin, customer-comm=jess, postmortem=ryan.
maria: i'll write and paste the runbook (mitigation checklist + audit queries + key rotation steps) in 15m. current AOs: netpol canary, RBAC SA change, KMS key rotate, enable audit shipping.
jess: i'll include step-by-step support instructions to capture `kubectl logs`, `kubectl exec`, and how to verify netpol enforcement.
kevin: after mitigations, add CI regression test to fail builds if an agent binary exposes a management port on loopback without auth.
ryan: agreed. postmortem owner is me; target public postmortem in 5 business days.
maria: updating SEC-2026-1893 and INC-2026-0789 after the canary run. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
